ROOMS OF THE KAPPA CHAPTER.

WEDNESDAY, May 5, 1875.

Afternoon Session.

The Convention was called to order
by Brother F. A. Brown,
President of the Executive Council, who appointed Brother C. L.
Clarke, of the Kappa, temporary, Chairman, and Brother C. H. Wells,
{Kappa) temporary Recorder.

The Chair appointed a committee of three on Credentials, con
sisting of Brothers Forrest {Zeta), Cobb {Psi), and Gay {Gamma).
Also, a Committee on Permanent Organization, consisting of Bro
thers Howe {Beta), Young {Upsilon), and Curtis {Kappa).

After a short recess the Committee on Credentials reported the
following delegates present :
Theta, F. T. Hastings, F. P. Johnson, and Thos. F. Quimby.
Beta, E. P. Howe.

Sigma, Rathbone Gardner.
Gamma, Moses Gay, John B. Stanchfield.
Zeta, Wm. S. Forrest, Chas. W. Whitcomb, E. C. Carrigan.
Lambda, George Sherman, Du Bois Smith.
Kappa, Will. J. Curtis, Geo. R. Swasey, A. Sanford.

4

Psi, Eben B. Cobb.
Xi, A. S. Underbill, G. S. Coleman.

Upsilon, F. W. Young.
Phi, E. H. Ranney, A. S. Higginson.
Omega, R. B. Twiss.

The Conimitte on Permanent Organization then presented the
following nominations :

President,

F. A. Brown, .{Lambda).

F. T. Hastings, Theta, Rathbone Gardner, Sigma.
F. W. Moses Gay, Gamma.
Young, Upsilon.
E. H. Ranney, Phi, G. S. Coleman, Xi.

Recorder,

W. G Waitt, {Kappa).

Assistant Recorders,

W. H. G. Rowe. {Kappa). Chas. T. Hawes, {Kappa).

The nominations were approved and the committees discharged.

The President, on taking the chair, submitted the Annual Com
munication of the Executive Council, which was referred to the
Committee on New Business.

On motion of Brother
Young (Upsilon), the report was read by the
Recorder.

The reading of the Treasurer's called for the
report was by
President.

5

On motion of Brother Forrest {Zeta), the reading of the report was

postponed until the morning session.

The President then appointed the following standing committees.

Committee on Unfinished Business.
Young {Upsilon), Swasey

{Kappa), Twiss {Omega), Underbill {Xi), Whitcomb {Zeta).
Committee on New Business. Stanchfield {Gamma), Sherman
{Lambda), Ranney {Phi), Forrest {Zeta), Curtis {Kappa).
Committee on Nominations for Executive Council. 
Howe

{Beta), Gardner {Sigma), Hastings {Theta).

Bro. Howe, as Chairman of Committee on nominations for Execu
tive Council, presented the names of the following Brothers as

nominees for
membership of the Executive Council for i875-'76 :
F. A. Brown {Lambda), George Zabriskie {Delta), Geo. C. Coffin

{Zeta), Fred. G. Dow {Kappa), H. W. B. Howard {Beta).

On motion of Bro. Cobb (Psi), the report was accepted and the
committee discharged.

Bro. Cobb {Psi), then presented a petition from members of
University for the establishment of a Chapter of Psi
Syracuse
Upsilon at that University, which was referred to Committee on New
Business.

Bro. Stanchfield, Chairman of Committee on New Business, intro
duced the following General Resolution No. i.

Resolved by Convention~of the Psi Upsilon Fraterhity,
the General
That the petition Chapter of the Fraternity at Syracuse
for a

University be granted; and referred to the Chapters for their con
sideration.

On motion of Bro. Howe {Beta), the Convention went into a Com
mittee of the Whole, to consider the matter referred to with regard
to the establishment of a Chapter at Syracuse University.

Bro. Howe took the chair. [In Committee of the Whole.]

The Committee of the Whole then rose, and through Bro. Howe

6

{Beta), reported favorably on this question. Voted a second reading
and passed.

Bro. Young {Upsilon), Chairman of Committee on Unfinished
Business, then presented the following items for the consideration of
the Convention.

I. The report of the Committee appointed to investigate the duties
and powers of the Executive Council, which was postponed until the

present Convention.
II. Report of Committee on Certificates.

Report accepted.

On motion of Bro. Gay ((?), it was voted that a
special com
mittee of three be appointed by the President, to consider the
establishment of a so-called Chapter at Cornell University.

The President then appointed the committee. Cobb
following 

{Psi), Stanchfield {Gamma), Smith {Lambda).

ness, introduced the following General Resolution No. 2.
Resolved by the General Convention
of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That a committee be appointed to select a
Fraternity color or colors.
On motion of Bro. Howe
{Beta), laid on the table until morning
session.

Bro. Young {Upsilon), then introduced the following General
Resolution No. 3.

Resolved by the General Convention
of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That each Chapler shall hereafter
prefix to the record of its mem
bers in the catalogue, the
day, month and year, on and in which that
Chapter was founded, and that the names of the founders be set in
italic type for the information of the
Fraternity at large.
Referred to Committee on New Business.

Bro. Young {Upsilon), also introduced the following General
Resolution No. 4.

7

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity,
That a Committee consisting of from each
one man
Chapter, (the
several Chapters to nominate and elect their representative), be ap

prize lists, honor men, total livingand dead members, total valuation of real estate owned the
by Chap
ter, programmes of regular exercises, time and

and all such detailed information as
may be of interest to the Frater
nity ; the same to be arranged and prepared for presentation to the
regular Convention by the Executive Council, and to be by them
published for the Fraternity at its semi-centennial in 1883.
Referred to Committee on New Business.

Bro. Stanchfield {Gamma), being unable to serve on Committee in
relation to Cornell affairs, Bro. Gay {Gamma), was appointed in his
place by the President.

On motion of Bro. Twiss {Omega), the Convention took a recess
until Committees were ready to report.

Bro. Swasey {Kappa), extended a cordial invitation to the delegates
to be present at a social gathering in the Hall in the evening.

On motion of Bro. Stanchfield {Gamma), the Convention adjourned
until 8 o'clock in the evening.

8

Evening Session.

The Convention was called to order at 8 o'clock, by the President.

Bro.-Stanchfield {Gamma), Chairman of Committee on New Busi
ness, then offered the following General Resolution No. 5.

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That the action of the Theta Chapter in initiating Messrs. Fitch and
Brown, was grossly careless, and in violation of the spirit of the
Constitution, and that they be censured therefor.

On motion ot Bro. Hastings {Theta), the resolution was laid on the
table until the morning session.

Bro. Cobb {Psi), then offered the following General Resolution

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That the Executive Council be appointed a Committee to devise
the best plan for incorporating the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, and to

report at the next Convention.
Referred to Committee on New Business.

On motion of Bro. Stanchfield {Gatnma), the Convention ad
journed until 9 A. M., Thursday, May 6th, 1875.

9

THURSDAY, May 6th, 1875.

Morning Session.

The Convention having been called to order by the President, the
minutes of the preceding meetings were read and approved.

Bro. Stanchfield, {Gamma), Chairman of Committee on New Busi
ness, presented the following General Resolution No. 7.
Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That the Chapter be censured for wilful ignorance of the
Beta
Constitution of '69, for violating it, both in letter and spirit, by the
initiation of Mr. Cluck.

On motion of Bro. Forrest, {Zeta), the Convention resolved into a
Committee of the Whole, to consider the affairs of the Beta and
Theta Chapters.
The Committee Tose, and through Bro. Young, Chairman, reported
favorably on General Resolution No. 7, as amended, and General
Resolution No. 5. Report accepted.
Bro. Howe thought the Beta Chapter deserving of censure, and
"
only objected to the word wilful."
Bro. Swasey {Kappa), agreed with Bro. Howe.

Bros. Forrest {Zeta), Underbill, {Xi), Gay {Gamma), and Twiss

{Omega), opposed the amendment.

General Resolution No. 7, with amendment, was then passed.

General Resolution No. 5, was voted a second reading, and

passed.

Bro. Cobb {Psi), presented the following General Resolution No. 8.

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That it is the of the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon
opinion
Fraternity, that a new edition of the Fraternity Song-book be issued,
and that proper action be taken accordingly.
2

lO

Bro. Cobb also presented General Resolution No. 9.

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity,
That the Executive Council be appointed Committee to consider
a

the advisability of establishing a Judiciary Board, to which all mat
ters under discussion can be referred for final decision.

These two resolutions were referred to the Committee on New
Business.

Bro. Stanchfield, Chairman of Committee on New Business, pre
sented the following General Resolution No. 10.

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity ,

That the initiation of Mr. Cluck, by the Beta Chapter, be pronounced
illegal and void.
Voted a second reading and passed. 

The Committee on New Business then reported favorably upon
.General Resolutions Nos. 2, 6, 8, and 9 ; and unfavorably upon Nos.
3 and 4. Nos. 6 and 8 were then voted a second reading and passed.

No. ir.

Resolved by the General Convention
of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That the Chapters of this use the names and the
Fraternity of
signs
the oflacers in their
correspondence with the other Chapters and the

Bro. Moulton {Kappa), Chairman of Committee on Certificates,
then submitted the
following report:
The committee
appointed by the Forty-first Convention to con
sider the subject of a
Fraternity Certificate of Membership, respect
fully submit the following report :
We have been
working under difficulties, for we have had no
opportunity to confer together. Still, the opinion of the members
has been ascertained
by correspondence, and we are happy to inform
the Convention that we consider a
Fraternity Certificate of Member
ship very desirable to advance and sustain the interest in our old
Fraternity. We have two designs which we present to the Con
vention. The first is designed
by Mr. F. R. Rathburn. The second

n

is the design which was used
by the Lambda. We are unanimously
in favor of a certificate from a steel plate, and recommend the Con
vention to pass the following General Resolution No. 12.

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That a committee of three be appointed to carry out the instructions
of this Convention in regard to the
subject of Fraternity Certificates
of Membership; said committee to consist of two members of the
Executive Council, the third to be some graduate member.

We think Bro. Geo.- W. Elliott, of the Xi '73, should be appointed
as the graduate member.

We also recommend that the Convention appropriate the sum of
$20.00 to pay Mr. Rathburn for his design.

Hoping that the designs will meet the ideas of the Convention,
I am, ^

Yours, fraternally,

WM. H. MOULTON, Chairman.

Report accepted, and referred to Committee on New Business.

Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
That the Executive Council be instructed toreport at the next
Convention an amendment to the Constitution, providing against

injurious action on the part of Chapters to the Fraternity.

On motion of Bro. Whithcomb {Zeta), a recess was taken, after
which Bro. Cobb. {Psi), Chairman of Committee to investigate
Cornell affairs, submitted the following report :

The committee appointed to make investigation concerning the in-

H

stituting of the so-called Pi Chapter of Psi Upsilon, at Cornell
University submit the following report:
We deem it advisable first to present to you the letter written
to the Convention in which they state the reasons for their
action. (The letter was then
read.) In addition to the state
ments in that communication the following facts were elicited from
the representatives from Cornell, Messrs. Noyes and Fulton.

I. That the action was purely and entirely that of the Psi Upsilon
alumni, at Ithaca; that the undergraduates had nothing whatever to
do with it, and that therefore all blame must be attached to these
alumni.

2'. That at that time, notwithstanding the fact that a complete copy
of the revised Constitution had been in their possession for about
five years, said alumni had no thought of acting unconstitutionally,
but that more recent investigation has convinced them of the illegal

ity of their proceedings.

3. That although the undergraduates previously initiated at the
Theta had perfect knowledge of this illegality at the time the abovementioned action was taken, yet they opposed it in no way whatever.

4. That the same undergraduates acknowledge that they have been
guilty of a serious mistake, guilty through ignorance, not through
any malicious intent. They now petition the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
in Convention assembled, to ratify their action for the welfare of the

Fraternity, and by so-doing retain in the society men who are now
possessed of all the secrets, and are perfect Psi U's, except as regards
legal initiation.
This your committee regard to be a correct statement of the case,
as
presented to them by the defenders of the action.

From these facts we draw the following conclusions :

First. That the alumni are without excuse, and that their plea of

ignorance is unwarranted, as a copy of the Constitution has been in
their possession for five years, as while undergraduates they were
members of the Fraternity and must have been conversant with the
requirements for the initiation of a new Chapter, and finally, as they
must have known of the repeated
rejection by the Chapters of their
petitions.
Second.^-Thz.t the whole action appears to be an unprecedented

15

usurpation by individuals of a power belonging only to the entire
Fraternity, therefore we offer the following resolutions :

General Resolution No. 20 
Resolved by the General Convention
of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, That in view of such wilful violation of
the Constitution, by the alumni concerned in this matter, that this
Convention instruct the several Chapters to which said alumni res
pectively belong to expel them from the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.

General Resolution No. 21 Resolved by the General Convention
of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, That in
regard to the undergraduate
members of Cornell University initiated at the Theta, they be

indefinitely suspended from active membership by their respective
Chapters.

General Resolution No. 22 
Resolved by the General Convention

of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, That the initiation of the men received
into the so-called Pi Chapter, by the above named alumni, be declared
null and void.

General Resolution No. 23

Resolved by the General Convention

of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, That the Executive Council be in
structed to publish in the Ithaca journals such a statement of the
case as they deem advisable.
All of which is respectfully submitted.

Cobb, (Psi) )\ Committee.
Gay, (Gamma)
Smith, (Lambda) \

Report accepted.

Resolved, That the thanks of the Fraternity be extended to Brother

Special 2

Special

Special Resolution No. a^ Resolved, That the thanks of the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity, in Convention assembled, be tendered to the

i8

mously by the Convention.

Brother Stanchfield, Chairman of Committee on New Business,
presented the following :
General Resolution 'i^O. 2$ Resolved by the General Convention

of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, That the amount of $20.00 be taken
from the Convention Fund to defray the expenses of the Committee

upon a Psi Upsilon Certificate.

Voted a second reading and passed.

Brother Forrest (Zeta). requested the Chapters to send to the Zeta
all Psi Upsilon songs in their possession.

On motion of Brother Young (Upsilon), the President then an

nounced the Forty Second Annual Convention of the Psi Upsilon
Fraternity adjourned, sine die.
FRED. A. BROWN,

President.
William G. Waitt,

(APPENDIX A.)

ANNUAL COMMUNICATION

OF THE

EXECUTIVE COUNCIL.
^tt.

To the Forty-Second Annual Convention of the Psi Upsilon

Fraternity.

The Executive Council would respectfully present their annual
communication.

It gives the Council great pleasure to congratulate the Fraternity
upon its continued prosperity. By the secretary's report it will be
seen many Chapters report an increase in the number of active mem

bers. While an increase in our numbers is not the chief object of our
Fraternity, it, nevertheless, shows a healthy activity in the Chapters,
and is an encouraging sign for the future.

The amendment to the Constitution passed by the last Convention
has been adopted by the Fraternity. The Council would recommend
further legislation upon this subject. The Constitution now prevents
the breaking up of Chapters without the consent of the Fraternity^
but does not provide for the protection of the Fraternity against in
In the early history of the
jurious action on the part of Chapters.
Fraternity, when there were fewer Chapters and less frequent inter
course between the students of different colleges, the action of any

particular Chapter was of comparatively small importance. Now,
however, no Chapter can violate the spirit or letter of the Constitu-

24

tion, or falter in its course of improvement, without at once demoral'
izing its sister Chapters. There should be some means of enforcing
obedience to the laws of the Fraternity. It may be difficult to devise
this object, but the Council
the proper legislation to accomplish
urge its consideration.

The Council feel compelled to again call the attention of the Con
vention to the lack of punctuality on the part of Chapters, in forward
and in payingtheir assessments. This delay makes the
ing reports
duties of the Council exceedingly irksome, and often comparatively
useless. The Council particularly call attention to the large amount
of unpaid taxes. It is impossible for the business of the Fraternity to
be carried on unless the taxes are paid. Money is needed and it is
unjust that some Chapters should be compelled to bear all the ex
calls of the Council
penses, while others are permitted to treat the
for the payment of their taxes with indifference.

The final report of the committee appointed by the Council to en
quire into the affairs of the Alpha has been laid before the Fraternity.

The Council have prepared to publish the new catalogue so long
needed by the Fraternity, and have asked the Chapters to forward to
the Council a list of their members. The expense is estimated at
about $1,500.

As the funds appropriated to defray the expenses of the Council
have been used up, the Council must ask for an appropriation from
the Convention.

The Council are compelled to call the attention of the Convention
to the affairs of the Beta Chapter. Early in the Autumn the Council
were informed that the Beta had initiated several ladies. Bro.
Howard, of the Council, visited New Haven to enquire into the case.
He reported that the ladies referred to had been taken into the Hall,
and had passed only a mock initiation. Further, that it was the
unauthorized act of a few individuals. Later, complaints were made
to the Council that a man named Cluck, from Cornell University,
had been initiated into the Fraternitj'^ by the Beta. The Secretary
immediately wrote to, the Beta for an explanation of this violation of
the Constitution. No answer was received by the Council. Bro.
Brown was then appointed a Committee of one to visit New Haven,
and to investigate the condition of the Beta Chapter. Bro. Brown
reported to the Council that he was unfortunate in the time of his
visit, it being examination week. Mr. Cluck, it seems, arrived in

I

^s

New Haven one
morning, with a letter from President White, of
Cornell University, to the Beta Chapter, asking them to take Mr.
Cluck into the
Fraternity. So far, all accounts agree. The A of
the Chapter said that
they examined their Constitution, and found no
prohibition of honorary members. Another member of the Chapter
said they found that it was
against the law to initiate a person from
another College, but that they got around it on some
pretense, which
he did not remember. At any rate, Mr. Cluck was
duly initiated that
same evening, and left New Haven the next
morning.
The Council have lately been informed that several persons at
Cornell University have established a so-called Chapter of the
Fraternity at that place. Circulars were sent to the Chapters in
forming them of the fact.It will be necessary for the action of the
Convention to be prompt and decided upon this matter, to convince
the guilty persons that our laws cannot be thus impudently violated
with impunity. The Council leaves the vindication of our laws to
the Convention. !

In accordance with the instructions of the last Convention, the
Council sent a Committee of two of their number to visit the North
western University. Their report has been laid before the several

Chapters.
The applications for new Chapters at Syracuse University, and at
the North-western University, laid before the Chapters for their con
sideration by the last Convention, were defeated.

The Council thus leave the affairs of the Fraternity in your hands,
Brothers of the Convention, confident that the several needs of the
Fraternity will receive your careful consideration.
FRED. A. BROWN,
